original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.
Extending a source-count census without naming a supplier/interface decision it could change; audit #2973 pruning concerns before relying on the affected predecessor exclusions.

actual_scope: Classify exact costs two versus three for every ordinary rank-two target on two roles over M_m(K), m>=3, over every field.
scope_change_reason: This takes the explicit rank-two case of Open next question 1 of PR4772 as a formal-alphabet side result. It does not extend the connector alphabet or price a native supplier.
bottleneck_link: A complete singular-target exact-cost classification in the relaxed algebra-valued alphabet. Rank two can require an extra paid call; the result supplies no native preparation or recursive invoice.
stop_rule: Stop at the first proved rank-two classification with a bounded exact replay; leave rank three, more roles and physical implementation open.
evidence: PROOF.md proves the all-field classification and attaining words. verify.py enumerates all 2542806 binary m=3 rank-two targets, checks the full-matrix criterion against the new classification, executes all 7644 exceptional words, and checks ten explicit finite-field/block cases and controls.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Which ordinary rank-three two-role targets over M_m(K), m>=4, cost two or three, and can any cost more?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This locates the next singular-rank boundary of the exact-cost problem.
open_questions.first_step: Take a named deficient 3 by m block pencil in a rank-three factorization and apply the cited two-factor criterion.
open_questions.blocked_by: The rank-one pencil lemma here does not classify rank-two deficient pencils.

open_questions.question: Can one literal native producer and consumer implement these formal factors at a useful complete cost?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Formal factor cost does not price a recursive supplier.

open_questions.blocked_by: Native preparation, restoration, precision, stock and complete invoice costs remain unknown.
